In the end, Watch Dogs 2 feels like an improvement over the previous game in the series. 
The characters are fun to play as and interact with, all of the hacking elements have a lot more depth and make more sense, and the world feels more alive and rich than ever before, design wise and graphics wise. However the game does suffer from mediocrity in regards to its shooting mechanics and stealth sections. 

Is it a fun game? Yeah, sure it is.

One of my favorite childhood games, and im glad to see it have a spike in attention. It ended up being a really freakishly accurate representation of the real world now, with companies like Flock and Palantir. F*ck Flock, f*ck Palantir, and f*ck the surveillance state.

A huge improvement over WD1. WD2 takes the hacking formula, puts a relevant "hacktivist" modern (and sometimes heavy handed hipster) spin on it, and outshines the first game in pretty much every way.

This game is at it's best when you DO NOT play it like GTA. It makes zero sense for a hactivist group to be running around gunning down people in the streets. Use your gadgets, RC car & quadcopter, hacks, stealth, and other hacking related things and you'll have a much better time. I found a good balance of non-lethal/lethal that I think makes sense and fits with the theme of the game.

First off, I don't equip any lethal guns. Only use the stun gun, paintball gun, stun grenade-launcher, etc. 
Second, don't just murder everyone every mission. It makes no sense to kill cops, security guards, civilians, or even most main mission targets. The only type of people I do anything lethal to are the gang members. I'll call other gangs in to cause shoot outs (its a hack you can do) and drop mini-explosives from my quadcopter drone and RC car. Aside from gang members, I take out pretty much every other enemy non-lethally (baring some accidents that tend to pop up during intense situations :D) and I think it makes the game feel a ton more real like you're a hacker instead of a murderer or thug. If you just run around murdering every one, the playful light hearted cut-scenes during/after the main missions don't even make sense.

The game has 3 different "styles" of hacker you can be (although if you play long enough, you will eventually unlock all skills). These styles are: Aggressor, Trickster, and Ghost.

Aggressor is the most obvious and brute force one. You basically blast your way through enemy bases/buildings/areas with guns/explosives and physically hack the mission objectives in person as Marcus while fighting enemies and their possible waves of reinforcements.

Trickster is in my opinion the most fun because it utilizes all of the various hacks and gadgets you have the most out of the three styles. You use your RC car and quadcopter drone to complete the missions by distracting and setting booby traps for enemies, remotely hacking objectives with your RC car, calling in cops/gangs to confront the guards in the areas you hack, etc. This style usually consists of parking Marcus at the edge of a mission zone (be it behind a fence or something) and sending your robots to do all the work. Its really cool because Marcus is never actually seen or in danger, and if your RC car or drone are blown up, you're still safe and can start over again. Like I said, IMO this feels like the most "hacker" way to play that fits with the game because you are using your full arsenal of tricks.

Ghost is fun too. It involves using hacks/gadgets that distract, disrupt, or generally just do stealth related things to get the objectives completed. You can jam comms, cause blackouts, then sneak Marcus into the mission area and hack the objectives while darting from cover to cover hidden. While doing this, you'll make enemies cellphones ring to distract them or make their earpieces blare static so they are "stunned" for a few seconds.

Now, the open world. This game's open world might be one of the most detailed, immersive, and convincing one I've ever played in. All of the NPC interaction, and the fact that the NPCs are constantly going about their routines and have detailed behavior really make the world feel alive because they don't just feel like some static placeholders in the background. They really made the playful and sunny San Francisco area come alive. The visuals and atmosphere of the world are top notch. There is always something going on around you, especially in the various tourist locations where a lot of NPCs are around at once. There will be dogs playing with each other, people playing guitar, doing yoga, etc, and they all react to you. Whether you bump into them, start to take selfies with them in the background, flick them off or dance with emotes, every NPC will interact with you, what you do, or other NPCs around them.

The story is fun, quirky, light-hearted most of the time, and full of awesome characters that each have a backstory and personality. You do actually feel like you are apart of a hacktivist group by the way Marcus interacts with these characters before/during/after the main missions throughout the story.

I had about 65 hours into the game by the time I uninstalled it the first time (before DLC came out). I did all of the main story, all of the side missions, a bunch of the repeatable co-op missions, and a ton of collecting research points. After trying each one once, I skipped out on the "mini-game" side missions like drone races, go-kart races, DriveSF (Uber), etc because they didn't really feel "hacker" in any way.

I have reinstalled, and bought both story DLC packs and am playing through them now. So far they are great, and feel like a continuation of the main missions in the base game in terms of quality and content.

Definitely recommend this game!

[h1][i]Common question asked considering games these days: Is the port any good?[/i][/h1]

[spoiler][b]YES IT IS! Ubi really nailed it![/b][/spoiler]

It runs quite well on my shitty PC than I actually expected. I get smooth playable fps on FHD around 35~45 fps with most of the settings on ultra. 
[b]My specs are: Intel i5 760, GTX 760 2GB, 8 GB RAM.[/b]

[h1]Story:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Prologue was meh and it didn't feel like an intro at all. 
[*] Story wasn't much, expected a lot more but come to think of it, WD1 story was a lot better than this one. 
[*] The finale mission didn't feel grand nor had any sense of accomplishment that you beat the game. WD1 at least had that feeling to it. 
[*] Character developement isn't that great. Each one looks like a unique stereotype with forgettable names and faces.
[/list]
I'm quite disappointed with the story. BUT that doesn't mean its a bad game at all! I generally focus on the story in every game I play, but I easily got distracted the game activities, roaming in the beautiful and interactive world of San Francisco that I forgot that story even existed in the game.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]

From here on the game truly shines, if you can forgive the story and the lackluster characters, the gameplay counters it back hard and makes it worth playing.
[list]
[*]There are many controls for you to remember now and it takes a while.
[*]Driving's improved and even at high speeds, the game doesn't stutter for me.
[*]Parkour is fluid and works as you intend to! Not wonky like those AC games.
[*]There are no towers, but restricted areas where skill points are waiting for you to collect.
[*] The missions are broken down into smaller tasks like go to x and hack y, rinse repeat and thats all there is to it. 
[*] But some main missions were really fun like [spoiler]hacking the satellites, controlling giant spider robot and bots[/spoiler],sitro tower, the beautiful new dawn facility mission, and a couple-o more.
[*]Personally I think stealth is very easy, like the detection is slow and isn't realistic. Too bad we can't move the bodies though.
[*]Mobile is improved a lot, looks just like in GTA, only more refined and lots of songs to suit the mood. Custom tracks aren't supported.
[*]Can manipulate vehicles to your advantages with just a button, really changes the gameplay.
[*]Deep Character customisation.
[*]Combat is okay not that bad as reviewers say.
[*]Can interact with people and animals in ways like making their Note 7 explode lol.
[*]Drone controls are a bit wonky at first but you can change its sensitivity to your liking. The game encourages you to infiltrate restricted areas with these and yea, it's fun.
[*] You can teleport back your drones instantly to you after getting a job done or almost getting caught by a guard, which really breaks immersion and not that challenging if you ask me.
[/list]
[h1]World:[/h1]
[list]
[*]It's lively, filled with people, animals, vehicles, activities, etc. and never looks dull even for a moment.
[*]Both Day and Night look amazing in their own way.
[*]World map is very short compared to other free roam games.
[*]Police are really a pain in the ass, they just won't give you a break!
[*]Can fast travel to many places around the world right after the prologue.
[/list]
[h1]MP/Coop:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Can seamlessly invade another player's game. Like there is this moment when I invaded someone's game and he was busy taking some selfies in a crowded street xD 
[*]You can use Quadcopter and get an arial advantage over the invader. 
[*]There are some other modes such as Bounty Hunter mode where you can go after players that anger the police (with more than 3 stars) and you can track them out, killing them by doing them a favor and getting rewarded in the process.
[*]Playing coop with random peeps online is cool, with emotes and all we can coordinate each other and make our moves like infiltrating a base, etc. Like one uses the drone to tag enemies and the other one does the job.
[*] There are too many online activities that you can play with your friends/random people online.
[*] There is also a 4 player coop mode where you can gang up with friends upto 4 and wreak havoc.
[*]Problem is the moment a friend joins your game, it lags badly. It's fine when I'm playing solo and invasion mode tho.
[/list]
[h1]Graphics:[/h1]

Watch_Dogs 2 has amazing graphics with many settings that will make your jaw drop, you could notice the significant changes over the previous one. Infact both are quite different if you ask me. Like WD1 was dark and gritty while this one is all colorful and cheerful.

The disappointing thing in here is the character models are so ugly af!

[h1][b]Final Verdict:[/b][/h1]
[i]There are problems that need fixing, but since it was launched recently, it's quite playable and not some complete unplayable mess. The lack of seriousness and low sense of danger makes this game different from the first one, because it feels like a combination of Saint's Row and GTA V lol. But it's definitely better than the first one if that's what you're asking. So what are you waiting for? Just grab it already![/i]

[h1]8.5/10[/h1]

After beating the main story and all side missions in Watch Dogs 2, I can happily say its a pretty good game. The stealth is fun, the gunplay is pretty good and there is lots to do. There is a huge tone shift from the first game, which may put people of that liked the darkness and brutality of watchdogs 1. This game has a much more bright and comedic feel than the last game, which will please some and not others, but overall I enjoyed it.

The story might not be quite as good as in watchdogs 1 and some of the dialogue is a bit cringy, but overall its a solid game and a good sequel, with improved gameplay, greater mission variety and a better and more colourful world to explore.

Worth playing but its not a 10/10 game by any means. I feel like it tried to be both safe, and outrageous in spots at the same time and it kinda damages the identity it wanted to give off to gamers. The irony for this game is storyline wise it feels more relevant to the real world then ever in ways that if the game released today reviewers would pan it for being too "on the nose." But it came out almost 10 years ago so that doesn't apply.
Some of my big Pros: 
-You don't have to "kill" people necessarily. You can stealth objectives, stun them, air shot them as options.

[h1] 💻 Description: [/h1]
Ubisoft has had a bad reputation over the years in terms of its game building strategy. There are times when they create amazing games and there are other times when they basically “milk” an already used concept. Having played Watch Dogs 1 in the past, my expectations were quite low since the promises made in 2012 E3 were not fulfilled. I have never said Watch Dogs 1 is a bad game (don’t get me wrong) but the franchise had so much potential that thankfully, I was able to see it with my own eyes in its current sequel.

[h1] 📖 Setting: [/h1]
[h3] Summary [/h3]
Having failed to manage Chicago’s city-wide infrastructure, due to the influence of our beloved Aiden Pierce, the CTOS (Central Operating System) which connects everyone and everything has been installed in San Francisco. This time under new management called [b] Blume. [/b] Even though the system has been upgraded to its newest version CTOS 2.0, it covertly brings harm to many innocent citizens of the city, including our protagonist. Marcus Holloway an intelligent hacker from Oakland, having been accused of a crime he did not commit, decides to work with the hacking group called [b] DedSec. [/b] Filled with ambition and pride his new purpose is to take down Blume’s influence over the city. 

[h3] Characters [/h3]
Watch Dogs 2 lets us embark on a thrilling adventure. The plot revolves around a group of outlaws whose actions and thoughts can be very relatable to our own. A big comparison to the “vigilantly arc” experienced in the previous game. The cast has a funny (sometimes goofy) personality, with clear motivations and an intriguing character progression. The conversations can indeed get a little bit “nerdy” and “cringe-worthy”, but it's those features that make the interactions unique and thus more memorable. The dialogue ranges from happy moments to very dark ones (depending on the circumstances) giving us plenty of material to reflect upon. The only downside in my opinion is the main “villain” of the story. 

[b] Lesser Evil? [/b]
As you will see for yourself during your playthroughs, there will be times when you going to question both sides of the coin. Many arguments reflected upon the “villains” have a very valid point. Of course, they engage in illegal activities (the same goes for DedSec) which is considered an evil approach. However, their cause (for me at least) is far more justifiable than the one which DedSec stands for. A feeling that seems out of place, since the game in my opinion has no intention to offer. Overall, the writing is enjoyable but not perfect. There are flaws and plot holes, which to be honest was expected because the game relies almost completely on its gameplay aspect.

[h1] 🕹️ Gameplay: [/h1]
Watch Dogs 2 gameplay-wise truly outdid itself for many reasons:

[h3] Hacking [/h3]
[b] Toolkit [/b]
The hacking feature of the game, the soul and core of the franchise, is challenged to its fullest potential. You can hack cars, lights, robots, phones etc. in many different ways, something that the Watch Dogs 1 experience lacked. Furthermore, the many newly added features such as drones, provide an amazing toolkit for stealth lovers. Most of the missions can be completed without even having to engage in any combat!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2896420429
[b] Limitations [/b]
The clever touch that Ubisoft added was the battery system. You have limited use of the hacking ability, a smart way which keeps in check the ending [b] god mode [/b] feeling. This way, you are forced to follow a more strategic approach during your missions, by focusing more on your upgrades, ability tree as well as stealth and hacking. The bar can be replenished though, so no worries.

[h3] Movement [/h3]
[b] Parkour [/b]
The parkour aspect and the fighting style, in general, feel dynamic and fresh, with newly added animations that left me speechless. Marcus does flips, tricks and many more moves that bring a smooth feeling when free-roaming.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2896419740
[b] Combat [/b]
During combat, you can notice many details that both the protagonist and the NPCs share. For example, when different gangs were fighting each other, 3 SWAT trucks came in immediately to protect the citizens. The wanted system in my humble opinion is very well made. The above-mentioned incident proves this statement.

[h3] Exploration [/h3]
[b] World [/b]
San Francisco is beautiful and vast with a colourful, warm aesthetic that pleases the eye even in the most extreme situations like police chases. Driving is smooth and fun, which can prove handy on many occasions with special tweaks that I won’t spoil. There is a variety of vehicles from the faster to the more humble ones, all easily obtainable on every corner of the map.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2896419293
[b] Interaction [/b]
The way the world is expressed in this game, compared to its predecessor is one of the biggest ways Watch Dogs 2 improved from the original. The NPCs finally feel alive and have a purpose. You even can pet [b] dogs [/b] for god’s sake! The freedom of choice is not negligible, as customization offers a variety of options that can please even the most demanding players. 

[h3] Difficulty [/h3]
The game introduced the newly added [b] Realistic mode. [/b] In other words, enemies become [b] smarter [/b] and more [b] accurate [/b] with aim. Their health is slightly raised but they take the same amount of damage as before. It raises the stakes, which will ultimately prove useful if you ever play online against other players!

[h1] 👁‍🗨 Visuals: [/h1]
Watch Dogs 2 has amazing graphics. For a game that's almost 5 years old, they hold up pretty well. Details such as the fog that occurs during a rainy day, create an atmospheric feeling that I enjoy watching. The only downside here is the character models. In my opinion, they could dedicate more time polishing the product, as cutscenes sometimes prove to be disturbing.

[h1] 🎧 Audio: [/h1]
The music provides a neat touch to the game. I still remember the time when the [b] Fortunate Son [/b] soundtrack was playing in the background, as I was heading guns blazing into the fight. Of course, there are some [b] skippable [/b] songs here and there, but the missions become more [b] fun [/b] and more [b] memorable [/b] with such additions as the one mentioned above.

[h1] 🗃️ Side Notes: [/h1]
Co-op remains among its least approachable and yet most buggy features, but let it not discourage you from giving it a try. There are the familiar invasions, bounty hunter modes as well as many online activities, where you can bring havoc either with friends or random people you meet online. Lately, the Epic Store has offered the game for [b] free [/b] to many players. As a result, online became relevant and thus more enjoyable!

The DLCs are good yet short. I advise you to wait for the [b] Steam sales [/b] before buying the whole package since the prize can be considered a little spicy.

[h1] 📋 Verdict: [/h1]
Watchdogs 2 deserves the title of [b] the [/b] perfect [b] sequel [/b] as it improves whatever came before it. The writing can be considered a delicate topic; however, the gameplay redeems the whole concept.

[h2]I really enjoyed the first Watch Dogs game.[/h2] Nearly six years later, it still remains one of my favorite Steam games. So when Ubisoft announced a new Watch_Dogs game in my hometown of San Francisco, I knew I had to play it. Unfortunately, I didn’t have a PC capable of running the game at the time, so it just sat in my Steam library collecting dust for years. Fast forward to today, and I finally got around to beating it. Here are my main takeaways.

[h1]THE LOCATION[/h1]

[b]Watch_Dogs 2’s San Francisco is an accurate representation of what people imagine living in  San Francisco would be like.[/b] This game's portrayal of San Francisco, however, is so inaccurate that it's downright insulting. Here’s a list of things that Watch_Dogs 2 got wrong.

[u]It's too sunny.[/u] In reality, the entire city is covered in a depressing grey fog. I shouldn't be able to tell where the sun is, let alone see the golden gate bridge. It's also really cold. The last time I went outside with less than two layers was years ago.

[u]It's too flat.[/u] San Francisco is covered in hills that make it very incredibly hard to go anywhere. It's should not be fun to drive around.

[u]The streets are too clean.[/u] In real life, the streets of San Francisco look like a third world country. When I walk around as Marcus, I should have to fear my own safety, as I carefully dodge human shit, used syringes, and broken glass. Speaking of broken glass...

[u]Too many nice cars and not enough broken windows.[/u] It's nearly impossible to park a car, grab a coffee and not have your car broken into and looted within 5-10 minutes, depending on what neighborhood you parked in. 

[u]The public transportation works.[/u] The lack of bus schedule delays, unexpected maintenance stops, and overall lack of chaos really broke the immersion for me.

[u]Not enough insane people.[/u] Throughout the whole game, I saw maybe 3 crazy people. This ratio should be more like 1 in 5.

[u]Too many guns.[/u] Guns are nearly impossible to get in San Francisco. I had to pass a background check just to buy a pocket knife, yet it seems like every low-level goon has an assault rifle.

[u]People run red lights.[/u] In real life, San Francisco has these fucking bullshit fucking shitfaced motherfucking red light cameras that record the license plate of any car that runs a red light and sends the driver a $500 fine. If Ubisoft implemented these fucking cameras, then maybe the stoplight hack would finally be somewhat useful.

[b]Now with all of the shade I'm throwing at [strike]San Francisco [/strike] Watch_Dogs 2, they did get a few things right. Here are some of my favorite features.[/b]

[u]The NPCs are r etarded.[/u] Man, Ubisoft really hit the nail in the coffin with this one. Whenever the security guard takes cover behind a glass table or the police drive their car into the bay to catch my boat, I'm reminded of every time I've ever used public transportation, and I enter a whole new state of immersion.

[u]Everything is expensive as hell.[/u] $65,500 for a plastic quadcopter with a camera sounds like a deal you could only get in San Francisco. $350 sounds like something people here would have to pay for an unremarkable hoodie. When I found out that my coffee was free, I had to double-check that Ubisoft didn't charge that 15 dollar Frappuccino out of my Steam wallet instead. I'm pretty sure that the free food and drinks thing is a bug, and it should be fixed ASAP. Other than that, the game’s economy is pretty accurate.

All jokes aside, this game captures the magic of San Francisco very well. Almost every landmark in the game exists in real life, and I was able to drive around the city without having to use the map.  There were many times that I got out of my vehicle to marvel at the details I never thought they would include such as a back alleyway that I occasionally walk through, or a tennis court that I use sometimes with my friends. Although I’m still bitter that they didn’t include my home, I’m not really sure what I expected to be honest. The game’s portrayal of San Francisco is still quite impressive, and I could probably justify buying this game for just the map alone.


[h1]THE STORY[/h1]

Watch_Dogs 2’s story is a lighthearted and cartoony take on a very serious issue as opposed to Watch_Dogs 1 which is a serious take on a by-the-numbers revenge story. While the premise of Watch_Dogs 2 is much more interesting than the first game, the game’s goofy atmosphere really takes away from the immersion and makes otherwise suspenseful moments fall flat. It’s a shame too, as the fight for internet privacy is a more prominent and serious issue than ever.

The same can be said for the characters as well. The characters are very well constructed and fleshed out, each having a distinct personality and design that make for memorable and entertaining dialogue. They aren’t bad characters, really, but the game’s light-hearted, silly atmosphere really makes the characters feel inauthentic or at least exaggerated. As a result, I only remember like two of their names. While the campaign wasn’t as heavy as the first game’s story was, it was still a good story nonetheless. 

[h1]THE GAMEPLAY[/h1]

	The gameplay felts solid. My only real issues were the occasionally faulty controls, but it could just be me who sucks at the game. Most missions can be completed in one of two ways, loud or stealth. While it feels satisfying to complete a mission in stealth, going in guns blazing is just as fun, if not more fun. This is mostly a tribute to the game’s satisfying gunplay. The weapons feel powerful and natural to shoot, and aiming feels good even if the game is a console port. Technically, you can play the game nonlethally, but the first thing I did after I beat the tutorial was unbind the taser and buy a real gun because I’m not a little bitch. (Yeah, that’s right William. Fvck your pacifist bull.shit.) I’m sure that pacifism is just as fun, but I lack the remorse to let anyone in this city live.

	While this game’s depiction of hacking is far from accurate, realistic hacking is incredibly boring and would make for horrible gameplay. The hacking in this game is simple and intuitive, and the line puzzle minigame while fairly easy, is still enjoyable. Unlike the first game where hacking takes more of a backseat to the open-world gameplay, Watch_Dogs 2’s hacking is featured much more prominently. Without spoiling anything, this sometimes plays to the game’s advantage, while other times it can be a nuisance when you just want to drive fast and pop heads. Driving in Watch_Dogs 2 feels a lot better than the first game. While I didn’t have any issues with the first game’s driving controls, I will admit that driving in this game feels a lot more natural. 


[h1]So is the game worth paying $49.99 for?[/h1] 

Uhh, no. A general rule of thumb is to never pay full price for a triple-A title that’s more than a year old. However, this game is definitely worth picking up on sale. Any price under twenty bucks is 100 percent worth the price of admission. In summary, this game is a solid entry into the Watch_Dogs IP, and I can’t wait for the next game.

[h1]The Friendly Neighbourhood Marcus[/h1]

The protagonist of the sequel to Watch Dogs is a much funnier person and this immediately sets the tone as we complete our first mission. This particular task sees Marcus (or Retr0) deleting his ctOS profile completely. This is his initiation at the end of which he is recruited by DedSec. The setting is now San Francisco and once again it's all about Blume infiltrating people's life via their ctOS 2.0. Marcus, with the assistance of Sitara, Wrench, Horatio and Josh, sets out to bring down Blume once and for all. Fans of the original will be happy to see T-Bone join the team later on.

[h1]Hipster Is The Way[/h1]

This very much makes people side with either the predecessor or the sequel. Personally, I prefer this version to the first. With Marcus the atmosphere is much lighter - it is not a tale of revenge, anymore, as it was with Aiden. This is not to say it's better - this is just a different kind of approach which was more to my taste. It's good to see Marcus's relationship develop with the others who all have interesting personalities. Wrench, for instance, wears a mask at all times while Josh would be your typical anti-social nerd - he is, actually, someone suffering from Asperger's. Dusan is our nemesis - current CTO of Blume whose introduction sees him participating in a yoga session. 

You'll immediately notice the many clothes available for purchase. Hundreds of them, all depending on the type of store you visit. Plus, you have apparel rewarded for completing missions and also those available as premium content (i.e. DLC purchase). Pawn shops are only visited for selling looted items and buying ammunition. Weapons can actually be made via our 3D printer installed at our HQ. These consist of military as well as DedSec graded weapons. The former are a bit stronger but the latter can be customised by applying different kinds of skins.

[h1]SF[/h1]

I assume San Francisco is recognisable for those having been there or simply living there. There is a city center area, then Oakland, the so-called Marin and even Silicon Valley. A lot of areas to discover including Alcatraz positioned roughly in the center of the map. Famous landmarks are already included in our smartphone via the Scout application. This requires us to visit these places and take a selfie. This is a fun activity which is not limited to these sightings - we can take a photo anytime (yes, even during missions with our mask on), anywhere. As part of the app's news feed the others from DedSec will make a comment. SF is quite big and the foggy Golden Gate bridge is definitely a place where an obligatory selfie is a must.

[h1]Apps, Levelling Up And Game Mechanics[/h1]

Missions are referred to as operations and are divided up into 2 parts. Main missions advance the story while side operations are there just for the sake of fun. DedSec aims to collect as many followers as possible in support of their organisation, therefore, instead of XP we gain followers for every operation or side activity we complete in the city. Reaching a certain value will result in levelling up (max level is 23) and we can assign skill points to purchase abilities.

Some abilities remain locked even if we have enough skill points (or as the game refers to them research points). They can be unlocked by searching for so-called key data all around the world. Also, the amount of research points needed to max out everything is way more than what we get in 23 levels - the game wants you to explore everything in San Francisco and find additional, hidden research points. Beside these we can find money stash, paint jobs and even special vehicles. There is a lot to do in Bay Area.

Gameplay remained the same i.e. we can apply the stealth approach or go guns blazing when doing an operation. Marcus also has a stun gun (and later stun launcher). Stunning enemies from a distance is great but you should note that the enemies will wake up after a while. Taking them down via the melee approach will make them go sleep for good. Of course, using cameras to trigger explosions is once again heaps of fun.

We have two new additions to our repertoire: a remote-controlled car and a drone (or quadcopter). The first is especially useful when looking around for collectibles (we'll access a lot of vents to get on top of buildings) while the drone comes handy when scouting around tagging enemies. Our little car can also interact with panels (something the drone cannot do) and can taunt enemies so it'll remain useful till the every end.

What about Marcus's abilities? They are pretty much the same; new additions include mass hacking options (disrupting all NPCs or hacking all vehicles to cause mayhem) and remotely controlling cars. Its fun hacking a vehicle making it approach you so that you won't even need to get close to it for a hijack. And when the denizens of SF wish to call the police you can disable their phones immediately. Hell, you can call the police on them or even send various gang members after them. This option to label people as traitors is especially useful when infiltrating restricted areas.

With Marcus we'll also be doing some parkouring and when it is not enough we'll hack forklifts or cranes to get to a higher ground. The freerunning is really great and almost all buildings can be climbed on looking for hidden collectibles. A side mission will require us to go around applying graffitis. 

[h1]Multiplayer And Optimisation[/h1]

Some new modes are introduced such as Showdown or Racing. Most are difficult to play as players are not really available for such sessions. But you can always find coop partners as there are a lot of coop missions to complete. Some are actually pretty challenging - I noticed this when I failed these operations. I realised that those with purple colour in our phone are not really meant for solo play.

Hacking invasion returns and it is now better than ever. With our quadcopter it is easier to look for the other hacker. Beside hacking we can also go around looking for bounties. When another player is chased by the police the A.I. lets us join and assist the police in taking down the rival hacker. We can also decide to simply initiate a hunt for us by uploading our criminal profile to the world wide web. With a recent update the armored truck challenge has been introduced - this is considered a bounty, actually. We have to steal a package and drive around while having max police alertness. Other players can also join in. This is the easiest way to earn a lot of money which you'll need if you wish to purchase all vehicles available.

As for graphics, the game looks tremendously beautiful (especially the day/night cycle changes and the fog effect when close to the Golden Gate bridge). It is, unfortunately, not optimised very well. You can see a lot of threads about crashing and stuttering in the Steam forums. Personally, I trusted my Nvidia-recommended options and set everything accordingly. Occasionally, my UPlay still notified me not having enough RAM for smooth gameplay. This was a tad bit disappointing.

[h1]Summary[/h1]

Watch Dogs 2 is a great sequel. The map of SF is quite big and there are tons of collectibles hidden and many side activities are available. We can participate in motocross, sailboat and even eKart racing and we can also drive around in a cab for some extra buck. For the two most exciting multiplayer modes (bounties and hacking invasions) there are still players available and there is a weekly ranking system in place for these with special rewards. I managed to unlock / find almost everything in 90 hours which is roughly 50% more than what I spent with the game's predecessor.

Watch Dogs 2 is the second installment in the Watch Dogs series and this time we take our hacking adventure to the bright and sunny San Francisco. 

Story:

Set three years after the events of the first Watch Dogs game, we now play as Marcus Holloway. San Francisco becomes the first city to install CTOS 2.0 which marked Marcus for a crime he has not committed. Infuriated by the injustice against him, he becomes a member of the local branch of Dedsec and joins the fight against Blume and other corporations in Silicon Valley. 

I wasn't a huge fan of the story in the first Watch Dogs game, I found it to be rather bland and by the numbers and the very bleak tone of Chicago made the game a slog to get through, but I still enjoyed my time with it. However the story of Watch Dogs 2 is slightly better, but comes with a new slew of issues because of the new structure. The main game follows on Dedsec trying to get followers so they can get computing power to take on Blume, To do that you complete missions taking down Blume's associates and other side gigs like fighting swatters, other hackers and gangs. 

The main plot point is you need those followers for botnet, but very quickly that plot point is disregarded and by the end completely forgotten. Also not to mention each story mission is like it's own little contained story with a minor cutscene adding into the overall plot. There is a clear cut villain in Dušan Nemec, but he barely appears in the campaign, mainly in a few cutscenes to remind the player he's still around. 

Another thing a lot of people didn't like is the brighter tone and the goofy characters. The story is usually pretty lighthearted with plenty of comedy, with a few semi dark moments thrown in. First the characters. I found most of them pretty likeable albeit they do come off as slightly cringy in certain moments, but overall I found most of them fun and I started to care for most of them by the end of the game. As for the story, it's overall decently written, with plenty of plot points still being relevant even today, although it's still not amazing. 

Graphics:  

Switching from the rainy and dark Chicago, we now explore the bright and sunny San Francisco. I honestly loved my time exploring all of the areas in the game. The colorful look and the bright visuals look pretty good, especially during the night when the city lights up and you're high up on a rooftop overlooking the skyline. 

The environments all look amazing, but the character models honestly don't. If it's not a main character, the character model will look slightly off and I know it would take a lot of time to develop good looking models for an open world game, but honestly they look so much worse than the main characters. Sort of like throwing Plastic Green soldiers into an environment with a highly detailed figurine. 

Audio:

The audio design is really decent. First of all let's talk about the soundtrack, which I found really delightful. There's a good variety of music and you will definitely find the tracks that speak to you the most. Also one cool feature added into the game is allowing you to put earbuds on. When exploring the world on foot you can use your phone to play music and once you find a song with Song Freak (a spoof of Shazam) you can assemble a playlist of the songs you liked and listen to them avoiding the tracks you didn't like. 

The voice acting is top notch. I think everyone does a fantastic job the two highlights being Wrench and Marcus, but even then everyone does a great job with their characters. All the performances are all great and most emotions are displayed clearly. The sounds for guns and cars are overall decent, although most cars sound roughly similar, the only difference being between normal cars and either sports or muscle cars, with normal cars having normal noises and muscle and sports cars having powerful roaring noises.

Gameplay:

The gameplay of Watch Dogs 2 is roughly the same to Watch Dogs 1, albeit with some changes. One of the most major things is you can now do a non lethal run of the game and honestly this was a big issue with community. Most people found the characters too innocent so running around and gunning people down, seemed like an issue to a lot of people and I agree. I did a majority of the missions with takedowns and the taser, only resorting to killing in two missions (if you played the game, you know the missions I mean).

Honestly, I found no issue in a non lethal playthrough in fact I found the extra challenge quite fun. When you knock someone out, there's ZZZ letters on their body and after some time they will wake up and walk around waking up their friends you knocked out as well and start patrolling the area.

Of course let's talk about the main thing these games are known for, which is the hacking. You have even more abilities than the first game and that allows for even more chaos and more opportunities when playing missions. Most of the major ones are back from the first game, but there's a bunch of new ones. For example one of the new ones is allowing you to hack cars allowing you to ram them into enemies and other vehicles when you're being chased. 

Alongside new additions you now have two drones that you can control to get to places you can't walk into or for stealth reasons. You have a drone to fly to check your surroundings marking enemies and looking around the environments and also you have an RC jumper which allows you can use to get through vents and also to hack into terminals you might no want to touch yourself. To explore the world you will use cars to get from place to place and the driving is alright. Sometimes when going too fast, you might lose control which might mess you in a chase, but overall it's better than the driving in the first game.

So now let's talk about the open world. Most people find Ubisoft games to be completely lifeless and the worlds boring to explore, however I found the open world of Watch Dogs 2 to be really good. Taking your time off and looking at the sights is absolutely amazing, but seeing the people interact with you and other characters is pretty impressive. When taking a selfie of a cool sculpture, a person might pass you and photobomb you. Also the NPC interactions with other NPCs are incredibly awesome to say the least. Walk around a bar ? You might spot a man puking on the ground after he had too much to drink, you might see a group of tourists looking at famous landmarks, you can witness people proposing to their significant other and this goes on and on. Whenever I spotted something like this happening, I found it incredibly cool.

The mission structure is also something I really like. In Watch Dogs 1, the missions usually boiled down to going to a location, hacking some stuff and or killing someone. In Watch Dogs 2, there's some more mission variety, especially if you decide to do the side quests. There's still plenty of going to a location, hack something and leave, but usually there's a ton of messing stuff up too, like stealing a movie prop car and racing it around the city. 

Verdict:

Watch Dogs 2 is a better game over the first one in every way. The story is more interesting, the gameplay is much tighter, the missions are more interesting and overall there's much more player freedom. Seeing the sights of the bright San Francisco is a highlight of it's own and honestly I had an absolute blast going through all of the missions in this game, while I found most of the first game slightly tedious. On a sale this game is super cheap and it will provide you over 30 hours of content for all missions and even more if you mess around with the side activities like racing and collectible hunting, not to mention landmark visits are an activity by itself.  This is definitely worth the money. 

Final Rating:
9/10

Watch dogs 2 is one of the best games I’ve ever played, and definitely a game I will never forget.

I was one of those people that didn't bother to play WD2 because I was soured over the experience with WD1. Since I saw it on sale, I decided to finally get into it after hearing some positive feedback from people I trust. It's a major improvement.

Pros
+ The world is more realized and lived in. Chicago in the first WD looked good but seemed empty with not much to do. It did replicate some of the neighborhoods I see everyday (I live in Chicago) but overall it was sort of drab w/o any personality. SF in WD2 is more varied in its layout and pretty similar to what you'd see if you were go to the Bay area right now. 

+ It's less serious. THank god. The protag from the first WD was a grumbling emo murderer that spied on his family. It was humorless and nothing stood out that differenciated Aiden Pierce from any other gruff voiced dude with a gun and an open world to explore. This one seems more introspective and leans into the neon "edgy"  hacker culture that is portrayed in TV and movies. It's not accurate but it's certainly more fun. The story isn't just a standard revenge tale. Under the silly veneer and the sophomoric humor lies a very mature story that seems ripped from the headlines. Should we be able to enjoy the convenience of tech w/o sacrificing our privacy? How far is too far when the authorities use data to circumvent the law? It's pretty compelling without submerging the player in a bunch of morality tales. It has a slight problem trying to balance the two extremes of silly and serious but overall I still enjoyed it.

+ I appreciate the devs for portraying a person of color as not a list of stereotypes but a fully realized character with a fleshed out story arc. I appreciate that progression in a AAA game. I'm 39 and I see how far this sort of characterization has come. Also shoutout to the voice acting in this game. 

Cons

- The gameplay is fun but after you unlock some specific powers, you feel underwhelmed by the lack of a challenge. Once you unlock the gang attack or police arrest abilities, you can use that multiple times to get yourself out of sticky situations, no matter what. Although it's pretty humorous to watch a bunch of Mexican gang members simply gain access to an FBI HQ to kill a target, it highlights definitely lack of balance between empowering the player and flooding the player with enemy AIs with razor sharp aim.

- The UI is confusing and incoherent. Why can't I pause while opening my phone? Why does it take 3-4 steps to get to the options screen? The only way to pause on the fly is by going to the map screen? When I open my phone, I lose several key controls so I'll have to pull over rather than choose a Scout mappoint while I'm driving. It's dizzying and it'll throw you off when you first start playing.

- There are some gameplay mechanics that are either too sloppy or not dialed down. The cover mechanics fights you every step of the way if you're in an area with a lot of things to hide behind. IN a crucial moment, you'll back up against a wall, exposing you to gunfire instead of going away from the gunfire. The police also suffer from the annoying rubber banding that open world game devs like to do. So if you're blocks away from your would be captor, you'd think you're home free until their car, defiant of any sort of physics, is able to run you down even though they've crashed into several cars. This is while I'm driving a sports car btw.

Overall I would recommend it. I havent jumped on the online portion but once I'm done with the SP, I'll give it a shot.

You can fast-travel to all of the locations from the beginning (except just a few story related ones). Speaking of weapons, it also has a lot of weapons, you can't buy them from shops though. I'll try not to spoil anything but you'll most likely need to gather a lot of in-game money to get your hands on your weapon of choice and your gadget.

There are lots of interesting and funny side-missions and activities as well. Like, drone racing, sailboat racing, go-kart races and motocross. There's always something interesting to do in this game and it never gets boring.

The story is good, not too believable but the game-play definitely makes up for it. You can replay every single main story mission and side missions you have completed using your new load-out and skills. You can customize your character with tons of new outfits and weapons (+their skins) but you can't customize your character's hairstyle, beard and mustache.

There are several radio stations you can listen to in cars, there are many radios in the world that plays musics and the news will talk about you after you've completed any major story mission. If you like any song that is playing on the world or in your car, you can easily identify the song from the within the game. There are some cool hidden things in the game that doesn't count towards your 100% progression and doesn't give a lot of clues but it's definitely worth checking them out for their epic rewards.

Uplay has weekly challenges for this game, if you're into that sort of thing. Some of them are easy, some can be annoying and some just seem impossible. Like escaping a bounty 3 times - police will be chasing you along with several other players. You can hide from the police but not from the players as they can just see your location on the mini-map as well as the world map and if you've gone too far away, they can just fast-travel to a location near you. Also bounty hunters (players) can spawn very close to you sometimes which makes it almost impossible to complete them.

But those are just a few negative things I can say about this game. It's really awesome, I'd happily recommend it to everybody.

An absolutely refreshing game in the open-world genre.

Watch_Dogs 2 builds upon what worked well in the first game (hacking, stealth system),
and removes all the stuff that was annoying in the first entry (being forced to climb towers to advance the story, grumpy protagonist, wonky driving). 

Higher up buildings now contain paint jobs for your weapons, vehicles, RC Jumper or RC Drone; Clothes or simply money. Nothing of which is required for progression. Some do hide Research Points which unlock skills, but there are plenty Research Points to obtain to get all the skills you want (I'm currently still missing 3 skills, none of which I am particularly interested in getting)
You can now also find special drivable lifts, that can help you reach higher spots more easily.  

Marcus is a much more likeable protagonist than Aiden was, but more importantly, this game has an ensemble of characters. And while the 'internet lulz' aspect may seem too extreme to some, for me it works perfectly. The whole world of Watch_Dogs is a spoof of our own (arising from the simple fact they can't use real companies - besides Ubisoft themselves). After doing a few missions (main or side) I loved returning to the hackerspace to have a few conversations over recent events. It made everything feel very real. The story itself is nothing special, but the little moments made me grow very fond of all these characters. 

And while I didn't particularly dislike the driving in the first Watch_Dogs, I still think this one presents an improvement.

And San Francisco is just beautiful and there's tons of stuff to discover. I prefer this much over the rendition of Chicago from the first Watch_Dogs. Firstly, WD San Francisco is actually bigger than WD Chicago and thus far much closer to the real life counterpart than Chicago was (Seeing as RL Chicago is actually larger than RL SF). 
I hope they choose another similarly sized location for their next entry and not something that can't be made justice with current technology like New York (I'd like Boston please).


Thoughts on the PC Port: I had a single crash so far, but the game runs flawlessly otherwise.  
With the settings recommended by GeForce Experience, I get 55+ FPS all the time, usually it hovers around 65. Sometimes during very fast driving it drops below 50 for a splitsecond. Game looks fantastic at these settings.

After roughly 52 hours I finished all main and as far as I know all side stories (these are not instantly marked on your map necessarily). This included me just messing around in the open world, collecting stuff or playing some multiplayer.
This doesn't mean I'm done playing, since I still have a few collectibles and ressource points to get. And then there is multiplayer, which is not something I usually enjoy, but the asymmetry makes it work for me. And so far I had no connection problems or any experience with cheaters.

Pay attention to my timer to see if the game holds me :)

I’ve always been a fan of hacker-themed content, but this game has everything I love: music (which I adore), hacker mechanics, interesting characters, stealth gameplay, an open world, and so on. The game designers really did an outstanding job; most of the missions are very diverse. This time, I wasn’t in a rush, I just enjoyed the gameplay, so completing the main story took me about 28 hours.

I also finally played through the DLC missions. They were quite fun and entertaining, and I really enjoyed them.

To sum up, I definitely recommend giving it a try. Sure, you might not like the cars physics because of the arcade-style handling, but the other aspects of the game are truly well done. A surprisingly great game trying to masquerade as a mediocre one. This game is incredibly IF you play it the RIGHT way. Here's how to do that: don't play this as an ubisoft stealth-action game, play this game as an IMMERSIVE SIM.

This game gives you a surprising amount of player freedom in how you approach and execute your goals. It hardly ever railroads the player into picking one of a select few play styles like the previous installment did. Instead, it gives you a wide variety of mechanics, exploits, hacks and skills to develop overtime which can be used in conjunction with each other in surprising and novel ways. Half of the fun of this game is literally just seeing if some hairbrained tactic you came up with will actually work (and it surprisingly does, very often in fact). If you play it this way and think creatively and outside the box, then this game is brilliant and will keep you coming back for more whacky adventures.

As far as the story goes, it's cringe. There's no other way of describing it. It's cringe worthy, it makes you feel second-hand embarrassment. Don't buy the game if narrative is a sine non qua for your enjoyment. It's literally boomers trying to write dialogue for 2010s era millennial Reddit users. If you think you just had a stroke reading that, don't worry, you're fine and yes, it really is that bad. Expect stale meme jokes (e.g. u mad?, epic win! you just lost the game!!1!). If that's too much of a hurdle to overcome then this game may not be for you. If you can look past that stuff though, it's a very re-playable and enjoyable hacking themed sandbox and you'll likely have a lot of fun.

8/10

Watch Dogs 2's campaign is secondary to the experience of roaming around its simulated Bay Area, getting into impromptu adventures, and interacting with its people. IMO that's a good thing, its story is centrist pop-culture snark roleplaying as leftist hacktivism; in my experience it doesn't diminish from the fun of moving around and finding new things. It's also greatly helped by the personality of its main character, which shines through even if you treat the story as background noise.

It's been years and the game still hasn't exhausted its mechanical value for me. Sometimes I'll fire it up with the goal of seeing some new scenery, racing through the wilderness, taking some selfies, finding a nice outfit, or inconspicuously ruining the day of some demonstrably awful person. Whether by accident or not, this game is great at supporting the generation of these stories, and it seems like it'll be a while before anything comes out that does a better job.

[h1][Review #11]
Watch Dogs 2[/h1]
Open World and NPCs: The open world is vibrant and colourful and NPCs have their own lifes. They have picnic at parks, vent out their anger by smashing cars along the road and have conversations and get angry at each other. You can send gangs to police and vice versa and will result in a firefight. I really enjoyed seeing the gunfights but then it gets repetitive quite quickly.

Things to do: You can do side and main story missions, taxi services with requirements, sailboat and motorcross race and go around the world taking pictures of attractive landmarks. I have no complaints about the activities except for the sailboat races. I fucking hate them because they are fustrating to play and get first place for.

Progression: You progress by gaining followers, which is earned by doing all of the activities above. As you level up, you gain research points which can be invested into your hacking skills to make it more powerful and versatile. Eventually you will have to find the rest of the research points by picking them up or hacking them in places scattered throughout the world, which I don't really like. Overall, the progression system in WD2 is quite good.

Combat: There are guns in the game but it is very limited and there are lethal and non-lethal options to play the game. You also have explosives and non-lethal versions of it. Gunplay in the game is mediocre at best. You can also melee NPCs when you are near them. Stealth is an option when playing the game as you create distractions and can possibly take them out without ever getting near them by hacking environmental objects.

Hacking: Your hacking skills ranges from ability to control forklifts and cranes to mass hacking individuals to distract a whole of them, cars to force them to move away from you and infrastructures to disable them. You can send cars flying off bridges or force police cars chasing you to smash into buildings or activate steam pipes to explode.

DLCs: Buying the season pass nets you 3 major DLCs. The first one gives a modified school bus that can wreak havoc in the world, and the second and third DLCs gives you new story missions to do. Each DLC also offers other side content.

Multiplayer: 3 basic modes. The basic co-op mode, the bounty hunter mode, where you enter someone's world who is currently on a level 3 wanted level or higher and try to neutralise them, and a hacking invasion mode, where you hack a player and try to not get detected while the hacking gets done. Buying the DLCs gets you a new difficulty for coop and a new enemy type.

Overall, I really enjoyed this game (except for the sailboat races). Definitely buy it on sale. Also, the fucking police is a pain in the fucking arse which keeps appearing when I don’t need them to.

[h1][b]Watch Dogs 2: Everything's Connected
[/b]
[/h1]
[b]This review contains no major spoilers.[/b]

[h1][u]-Overview-
[/u]
[/h1]
[i]Watch Dogs 2[/i] is the sequel to the original Watch Dogs. It's set in San Francisco, a good-looking city, that has little representation in this genre, apart from GTA: San Andreas back in 2004. In the metropolis, everything's connected with the new ctOS 2.0, a computer system originally designed to manage the infrastructure of Chicago during the events of the first Watch Dogs. CtOS 2.0 is an improved version of it. The story focuses on a group of young characters who want to change society. You assume the role of Marcus Holloway, who joins a group of young hackers named DedSec to take down Blume, the corporation who invented ctOS. You don't need to play the first game to experience Watch Dogs 2, as it focuses on totally different characters in another city.

[h1][u]-Summary-
[/u]
[/h1]
[table] [tr] [th] ▼ Cons [/th] [th] ▲ Pros [/th] [/tr] [tr] [td] 1. Questionable level design in some missions
2. Sometimes invasive UI
3. Amendable driving [/td]

2. Overall good gameplay and hacking system
3. Stealth mission design is well done
4. Nice soundtrack and radio stations
5. Detailed and advanced skill tree [/td] [/tr] [/table]

[h1][u]-Deep Analysis-
[/u]
[/h1]
[h3] ▲ Pros
[/h3]

[b]1. Visuals[/b] 
There have been only a few times where I've been totally immersed in a game's environment, and Watch Dogs 2 is one of these cases. San Francisco here is alive, technological, and stunning to look at. Whether you're crossing the Golden Gate Bridge, or doing parkour to reach the peak of high buildings, the city always looks gorgeous. It is also full of secondary quests and side activities to do. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2446407622

[b]2. Gameplay[/b] 
The gameplay of Watch Dogs 2 is well-crafted and can bring you many hours of fun, most of it definitely comes from the hacking system. In this game, everything revolves around hacking. Unlike in games such as GTA, it's recommended to think of a good plan before going on a mission. In fact, if you're good enough, you can play almost every mission silently. There are two devices (apart from your smartphone, which takes care of most of the hacks) that can help you a lot in planning the best way to do a mission. The first one is called the Jumper, and the second one is the Quadcopter.
The Jumper is a ground drone, and it's the most useful object in the game. It can help you spot enemies and analyze the place of a mission before physically going there. It can also unlock doors, getting special permissions, and complete many mission objectives. However, it can also be easily spotted, so you have to be careful when going around with this little thing. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2471041185 
You can do the same with Quadcopter except it can fly.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2471041104 

[b]3. Stealth System[/b] 
As previously mentioned, thanks to the hacking system and some other useful tools such as the taser, you can do a lot of missions without getting your hands dirty. To get the best possible result, you have to use a combination of all the gadgets you have at your disposal. While the Jumper and the taser are available from early on, the Quadcopter is a device you have to buy separately with ingame currency. I'd recommend getting it as soon as possible. 

[b]4. Soundtrack[/b]
I really liked the soundtrack of this game. There are many good songs, even famous hits, all available while you're driving or through the Media Player app on your phone. You can listen to them anytime you want. Not all of the songs are unlocked from the start, but you can unlock other ones through Soundcloud, an app on your smartphone similar to Shazam, which recognizes new songs and directly adds them to the Media Player app.

[b]5. Skill Tree[/b]
The ability tree in Watch Dogs 2 features a nice and varied set of skills you can unlock or improve to push your hacking, aim, or driving to the ultimate level. There are a lot of cool options, for example you can unlock a massive hack that causes all cars to go hay-wire. Crazy!

[h3] ▼ Cons
[/h3]

[b]1. Level Design[/b]
Now, it may be me..but in some cases, the level design was quite confusing. A few times, I didn't know what I should do, or where I should go, and had to go to YouTube to find out. I don't consider this a major flaw, but still I had to talk about it. 

[b]2. Invasive UI[/b]
If there's something I dislike about this game, it's about the UI. I think that overall it's really great, but sometimes it becomes too much invasive for my taste. For example, there's a persistent white dot at the centre of the screen and I don't know why it's there. When you're driving a car, it's still there. I was annoyed by it and decided to install a mod to remove it, and nothing changed in my gameplay, so I really can't understand why they did that. Then, there's a skill which lets you know when some random NPC has a lot of money in his bank account, so you can hack it. However, the way the game notifies you of that is quite annoying. It shows four blue lines in the form of a square around the NPC, and that thing lasts quite a while. The problem is that the game notifies you of it even when you're inside of a building and you can't see the NPC, or when you're on a mission, and once you unlock the skill, you can't disable it. If you're annoyed by this kind of things, you'll probably be bothered by this one too, but once again.. it's not that big of a deal.

[b]3. Driving[/b]
I feel like the driving in Watch Dogs 2 is too much arcade-ish. I don't really know how to describe it, but it's like if some vehicles are too slow and others are too fast. The maneuverability of cars is almost the same for every vehicle, and the only thing that changes with different ones is just the speed and the design of them. It's worth noting though that it's not an issue that ruins the experience too much.

Way better than Legion. Cool story, mechanics and tech.  It felt like playing GTA but with the touch of tech/hacking stuff.

Keeping in mind, I try to not judge a game based on it predecessor, this was a good game that lost the spirit of the first game.  While yes, this was a fun romp and stomp kind of a game, the story was nowhere as good as the first one.  Watch_Dogs 1 had mystery and heart, it was a mature and dark game, and then this sequel got rid of that by essentially combining Saints Row with Watch_Dogs, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it is jarring if you've played the first, and don't already know what you are getting into.

Combat is fun, and has potential to be fast paced and overwhelming, depending on how you scope things out or if you just kind of blindly run in.  There is a number of things you can do to make the tide of battle end in your favor with hacks, between exploding environment pieces, very basic remote control of cars (single direction), and hacking enemies coms to stun them, but not a lot of variety there.  Mostly comes down to normal cover based combat.

Losing enemies can get frustrating, especially early on, since enemies and cops have a tendancy to have telescoping vision at times, and like to spawn with line of sight on you.  The helicopters can make it more difficult if you have gained enough attention to warrent one, and I had one point spent 20 minutes straight trying to escape the cops but couldn't because it was early game and I had no helicopter hack yet and it always knew where to find me, whether I broke line of sight and changed directions or not.  Later on, there were more than a few times I lost the noteriety without even knowing why.  Otherwise, it comes down to finding a corner where you can hunker down out of sight.

Stealth isn't bad, though could be better.  It boils down to mostly using your drones, since they are less likely to be spotted, and you'd have to use one for something out of full bodied Marcus's reach.  If they do get spotted, you can either just pull them out quickly, or if they manage to get destroyed, which they only take a single hit, have to wait (I am guessing 30 seconds base time) to pull out another.  Most of the time, you can just drop Marcus off, just outside the restricted zone, and let your drones do the work, as there is little the drones cannot do that Marcus can.

There are a lot of upgrades that you can get through progression and collection, and a lot of them felt kind of useless, in fact I think I might have barely used many of them.  There are "botnet" upgrades (botnet being the resources you use whenever you use certain hacks), but I don't see any reason why you would need as many as you can get. A number of upgrades I only got to screw around, while they did have a use, it just happened to work better pulling out your drones in those cases.  In fact, there were occasions when I tried to summon gang members on someone, and they gave up before even showing up.

The story (with minimal spoiler) essentially comes down to main character Marcus gets initiated into hacktivist group Dedsec, to take down evil corperation, Blume, who basically uses technology which is in absolutely everything at this point to spy and profit off of you by selling private and personal information to other companies who also use it for personal gain.  The members of Dedsec are memorable for the most part, other than Horatio (the kind of slipped him in and assumed I would care about him), as well as entertaining.  The problem is that I have a hard time seeing them as good guys when they act as a terrorist organization more than a hacktivist group.  I did enjoy listening to most of the characters, as they were all entertaining, even antagonist Dusan (or however his name is spelled).  It is something that I do like to see in games and stories, is an antagonist that I don't need to hate, while that would help make me feel the protagonists motivations, it makes me enjoy having scenes with him pop up.  The final scene with him didn't really make a lot of sense to me, as he just feels like he went from in control to feeling lost from one scene to the next.

The missions were okey, but tends to really shine in the DLC missions.  While the story was lacking for the main game to me, and the main missions pulled things along, the DLCs were more entertaining, and more engaging for me.

Technically speaking, I've heard a lot of people having issues with stuttering and whatnot, my computer which appearently didn;t make the minimal recommondations ran it just fine, though I didn't boost the graphics at all.  I had only one CTD in my entire playthrough, which is a lot better than I could say for the first Watchdogs.

All in all, if you are looking for a game with a strong story, this may not be the one for you, however as more of a simple goof off kind of game, it is an entertaining one.  While I would have liked the story to have more depth, the rest of the game.
